title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 181 (Company to contribute to bona fide and charitable funds, etc.)

content.overview: Section 181 provides that the Board of Directors of a company may contribute to bona fide charitable and other funds: provided that prior permission of the company in general meeting shall be required for such contribution in case any amount the aggregate of which, in any financial year, exceeds five per cent of its average net profits for the three immediately preceding financial years.
content.glance: Board may contribute to bona fide charitable and other funds; prior ordinary resolution of the company required if the aggregate in a financial year exceeds 5% of average net profits of the three immediately preceding financial years.
content.study: The Board of Directors of a company may contribute to bona fide charitable and other funds: Provided that prior permission of the company in general meeting shall be required for such contribution in case any amount the aggregate of which, in any financial year, exceed five per cent of its average net profits for the three immediately preceding financial years. The section is a Board power with a member gate above the threshold. It is distinct from corporate social responsibility under section 135, which is mandatory for companies crossing the CSR net-worth, turnover or profit thresholds and is confined to activities specified in Schedule VII. Current-law framing: confirm the contribution is to a bona fide charitable or other fund; compute the 5% of average net profits threshold; require prior ordinary resolution if the aggregate for the year exceeds that threshold.

sections.heading: Board Power
sections.body: The Board may contribute to bona fide charitable and other funds.

sections.heading: Member Gate
sections.body: If the aggregate contribution in a financial year exceeds five per cent of the average net profits of the three immediately preceding financial years, prior permission of the company in general meeting (ordinary resolution) is required.

sections.heading: Distinction from CSR
sections.body: Section 181 is permissive Board giving subject to a member threshold. Section 135 CSR is a mandatory spend for companies meeting statutory thresholds, directed to Schedule VII activities.

provisions.title: Company to contribute to bona fide and charitable funds, etc.

examples.title: Below threshold
examples.body: Average net profits for the three preceding years are ₹2 crore. The Board contributes ₹8 lakh (4%) to a bona fide charitable fund in the year. No prior general-meeting permission is required under s. 181.

examples.title: Above threshold
examples.body: The same company proposes a further contribution that would take the year’s aggregate above 5% of average net profits. Prior ordinary resolution of the company is required before that contribution.

hypotheticals.question: Does compliance with s. 181 satisfy the company’s CSR obligation under s. 135?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 181 authorises voluntary charitable contributions subject to a member gate. Section 135 imposes a separate mandatory CSR framework for eligible companies. One does not substitute for the other.

distinctions.title: Charitable contributions (s. 181) vs CSR (s. 135)
distinctions.left: Permissive Board power with 5% average-net-profits gate
distinctions.right: Mandatory CSR spend for threshold companies on Schedule VII activities

misconceptions.trap: Every charitable contribution needs a general-meeting resolution.
misconceptions.correction: Only the aggregate that exceeds five per cent of average net profits of the three immediately preceding financial years needs prior permission of the company in general meeting.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm bona fide charitable/other fund. II. Compute 5% of average net profits. III. Require prior ordinary resolution if exceeded. IV. Distinguish CSR. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Contribution facts; threshold calculation; resolution status; precise relief.
